title: How the website knows it is you
concept: Sign-in explained in plain words; automatic in the game

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: One question people always ask: how does the website know you are allowed to push?

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: On a real computer you sign in once. A window opens in your browser and you approve it.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: After that your computer remembers, and push and pull just work.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: In this game sign-in is automatic. There is nothing to set up.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Two quick checks, then we do the chapter boss.

hints: These are reading questions. Look back at what Ada said.
Sign-in happens once per computer, in the browser, and then git remembers.
Pick "Once, in the browser" and "Nothing: it is automatic in this game".

questions.prompt: On a real computer, how often do you sign in to the website for git?

choices.text: Once, in the browser, then the computer remembers

questions.explanation: You approve it once per computer. After that git reuses what was saved.

questions.prompt: What do you have to set up for sign-in in this game?

choices.text: A password file in the repo

questions.explanation: The game signs you in for you so you can focus on git itself. Never put a password in a repository.

recap: On a real computer you sign in to the hosting site once, through your browser. In this game it is automatic.
